findings.title: Steer-race follow-up for a question notice runs on the composer model, while the steered copy and a mailbox follow-up use the parent run's model
findings.body: When a question notice is steered, `Orchestrator.ts:5837-5840` pins its model selection to the target run's selection, as it does for a delegated completion. If the steer loses the race with turn completion, the retry here passes `modelSelection: run.modelSelection` only when `message.delegatedCompletion !== undefined` (lines 295-297). A notification-only message therefore starts its new turn with the thread's current composer selection. The new test pins that behaviour at `SteeringCompletion.integration.test.ts:433-434`, where `started[1].modelSelection` equals `composerSelection`. The same notice thus runs on one model if the steer lands and another if it loses the race. A plain queued notice already uses the thread selection, so this may be intended. Is it? If it is, say so in a one-line comment. If not, pass `run.modelSelection` for notifications too.

contracts.action: Steer a delegated-task question notification into the running parent turn instead of queueing it behind that turn
contracts.equivalent_path: The existing delegated-completion mailbox routing in the same block (Orchestrator.ts:5739-5775) and the `steer_active` branch that calls `dispatchSteerIntoRun` (5830-5858).
contracts.before_after: Before: only mailbox completions with completionWake 'always' were upgraded to steer_active, and a question notice stayed queue_after_active. Now: a notification with source.kind 'delegated_task' takes the same upgrade, requiring a running run, a running provider turn, a live session that supports active steering without interrupting tools, and (new) no Stop having reached the run. The steered message keeps the target run's model selection (5837-5840) and skips the thread selection update (4942-4944). `dispatchSteerIntoRun` stores the notification on the message and emits `notificationTurnItem` (4842, 4911). The Notifications-must-be-queued validation (5680-5695) runs before the upgrade, so it still sees queue_after_active.
contracts.visible_effect: The parent agent sees the child's question during its current turn. The notification card shows in the parent thread's turn items. Only DelegatedTaskQuestionReactor emits kind 'delegated_task' notifications outside tests (DelegatedTaskQuestionReactor.ts:49-52), so no other flow is rerouted. The new `stopReachedRun` guard also applies to mailbox completions. It avoids the 'is stopping and cannot be steered' dispatch error at 4747-4753.
contracts.failure_mode: If the steer is rejected because the turn completed, the EffectWorker catch re-dispatches the message as queue_after_active (EffectWorker.ts:282-299). Before this change a notification-only message was re-dispatched as start_immediately and was rejected by the validation at Orchestrator.ts:5681-5689. A steered question cannot be cancelled when the user answers it first, unlike a queued one. The notice text covers that case ('If it is no longer pending, it was answered or dismissed').

contracts.action: Retry a failed steer of a notification message as a queued dispatch
contracts.equivalent_path: The existing delegatedCompletion retry in the same catch block, which already used queue_after_active and passed `notification` through.
contracts.before_after: Before: only messages with a delegatedCompletion were retried as queue_after_active. Notification-only messages got start_immediately and failed the notification validation. Now: `queued` covers both kinds, and the message's notification is forwarded (lines 306-308).
contracts.visible_effect: A question notice that loses the steer race still starts a follow-up turn on the parent, and the test checks that exactly one notification item exists.
contracts.failure_mode: The retry reuses the message id and uses command id `command:steer-follow-up:${effect.id}`, so a repeated effect run cannot duplicate the message. A disabled provider instance is logged and dropped (EffectWorker.ts:317-329).

summary: I found no defects in this change. Question notices from delegated tasks now steer into a running parent turn, and a notice that loses the steer race is retried as a queued message. One question for the author: after a lost steer race, the retry runs the notice on the thread's composer model, not the parent run's. The steered copy and a mailbox completion use the run's model, and the new test pins the composer model at `SteeringCompletion.integration.test.ts:433-434`. The doc paragraph matches the code. I only read the code; I did not run the tests.
